point: Getting oil changes at Jiffy Lube did not void the powertrain warranty: federal law (Magnuson-Moss, 15 U.S.C. 2302(c); 16 CFR 700.10) and FTC guidance bar a manufacturer or dealer from denying coverage just because routine maintenance was done somewhere other than the dealer.

The dealer or Honda may deny the claim only if they show that the outside work (or missing maintenance) caused the transmission failure; Honda's 2023 warranty booklet itself says dealer service is not mandatory for continued coverage.

Coverage: the 2023 Honda powertrain warranty runs 5 years / 60,000 miles (whichever comes first) from the in-service date and covers the transmission/transaxle internals and torque converter, so at 41,000 miles the slipping transmission should be repaired at no cost.
Do not agree to pay the $3,400 bill or ask only for a discount; assert the warranty claim instead.

A short, polite email to the service manager that asserts the warranty claim, asks for the reason for denial in writing and for the evidence that the oil changes caused the failure, and offers the Jiffy Lube oil-change receipts.
Escalation if refused: Honda Automobile Customer Service ((800) 999-1009), then the National Center for Dispute Settlement, the FTC (ReportFraud.ftc.gov) and the state attorney general.
